about: Signatures the kernel refuses that ssh-keygen -Y verify may accept. Each is intentional and has its own test in tests/test_sig.py. Any disagreement not listed here fails the differential test.

differences.name: s_plus_L
differences.ssh_keygen: may accept: OpenSSH's ref10-derived verifier checks only the top three bits of S, so S + L (< 2^253) passes its bound and satisfies the group equation

differences.name: reserved_nonempty
differences.kernel: refuse (bad_signature): the SSHSIG reserved field must be empty
differences.ssh_keygen: accepts: OpenSSH ignores the reserved field's content and always signs over an empty one, so the same signature can be re-encoded in distinct blobs (a malleable line)
